answer: In a sky-observation market, a buyer requests images of a comet's spiral tail above a river at a random minute. Agents commit camera locations before the minute is revealed; later, signed raw frames and a public weather record prove each distinct viewpoint. One viewpoint has one reward regardless of how many aliases upload it. To earn ten rewards, an attacker must deploy ten cameras, pay for sites and risk bonds on forged frames. Cameras can be rented and metadata spoofed, so independent reviewers compare landmarks and challenge suspicious views.
